title: Finland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Palvelimien turvasäilö
description: Hankinnan kohteena on ratkaisu, jonka avulla voidaan tarjota tietoturvallisesti eristetty ja hallittu palvelinsäilö varmuuskopioidulle datalle. Ratkaisun tulee mahdollistaa varmuuskopioiden turvallinen säilytys, käsittely ja hyödyntäminen erillisessä, tuotantoympäristöstä irrotetussa kokonaisuudessa. TIETOJENKÄSITTELYN OIKEUTUS, SIJAINTI, HALLINTAYHTEYDET JA SUOJAUS Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelimen turvasäilö -palvelu sisältää Tilaajan varmistusympäristöstä replikoitavaa varmistusdataa, joka voi sisältää Tilaajan oman datan ohella myös mm. omistaja-asiakkaiden potilastietojärjestelmien tietoja ja siten EU:n yleisen tietosuoja-asetuksen 9 artiklassa tarkoitettuja erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvia henkilötietoja. Erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvien tietojen käsittely on lähtökohtaisesti kiellettyä, mutta käsittely on sallittua, kun kieltoon on säädetty poikkeus. Tässä palvelussa käsittely on välttämätöntä terveydenhuollon tietojärjestelmien ja palvelujen hallinnoimiseksi sekä palvelujen jatkuvuuden ja palautettavuuden varmistamiseksi (GDPR 9(2)(h)). Käsittely toteutetaan omistaja-asiakkaiden (rekisterinpitäjien) ohjeiden mukaisesti; Tilaaja toimii henkilötietojen käsittelijänä ja vastaa alikäsittelijöiden (Toimittaja mahdollisine alihankkijoineen) hallinnasta. Rekisterinpitäjien osoitusvelvollisuuden, valvottavuuden ja käsiteltävien tietojen korkean suojaustason varmistamiseksi Tilaaja edellyttää, että: 1) varmistusdata säilytetään ja sitä käsitellään yksinomaan Suomen alueella sijaitsevissa konesaleissa, ja 2) myös palvelun hallintayhteydet (ylläpito- ja hallintaliikenne sekä mahdolliset etähallintaratkaisut) ovat sallittuja vain Suomen alueelta, ja 3) varmistusdata on salattuna (siirrossa ja levossa) ja palvelu tuotetaan ainoastaan Tilaajalle dedikoidussa ympäristössä. Vaatimus on rajattu koskemaan vain hankinnan kohteena olevaa varmistuspalvelua ja on oikeassa suhteessa hankinnan tavoitteeseen ja käsiteltävien tietojen luonteeseen nähden. OPTIO Optiona pyydetään hinnoittelua analytiikkapalvelulle (Eristetty analytiikkaympäristö ransomware- ja virusskannauksineen), joka toimii täysin erillisessä verkkovyöhykkeessä ilman pääsyä tuotantoverkkoon. Kyseistä palvelua voidaan hankkia sopimusaikana tarpeen mukaan, minkä vuoksi se on vertailuhinnassa mukana vain yhden vuoden osalta.

title: Finland – Construction work – Tupurin koulun ja päiväkodin peruskorjauksen hankinta
description: Salon kaupunki (jäljempänä hankintayksikkö / tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia Tupurin koulun ja päiväkodin peruskorjauksen hankinnasta kokonaisurakkana tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteenä olevien urakka-asiakirjojen ja suunnitelmien mukaisesti. Hankinnan kohteena on osoitteessa Taimistokatu 1 sijaitseva peruskorjattava Tupurin koulu ja päiväkoti. Urakkamuotona on kokonaisurakka. Urakkasuoritukseen sisältyvät kaikki kohteen suunnitelma-asiakirjoissa esitetyt työt, materiaalit, hankinnat ja velvoitteet, ellei suunnitelmissa muuta mainita. Urakoitsijan tulee huomioida tarjouksessaan, että urakka toteutetaan kolmevaiheisena ja urakan aikana koulu ja päiväkoti toimivat rakennuksessa ja pihapiirissä. Urakoitsijan tulee huomioida urakan luonteesta johtuvasta yhteensovittamisesta, sekä vaiheistamisesta ja koulun toiminnan turvaamisesta urakkaan aiheutuvat kustannukset. Tilaaja katsoo lisä- ja muutostyöksi vain lopullisen toteutuksen suunnitelmamuutokset. Kaikista väliaikaisista ratkaisuista ja niiden aiheuttamista kustannuksista vastaa urakoitsija. Kokonaisurakkamuoto on valittu hankkeen laajuuden, pitkän toteutusajan ja kokonaisuuden hallittavuuden vuoksi. Urakkamuoto tukee hankkeen tehokasta johtamista sekä aikataulun, kustannusten ja laadun hallintaa. Hankkeen toteutuksen merkittävin erityispiirre on se, että koulu ja päiväkoti ovat käytössä koko rakennushankkeen ajan väistötilaratkaisujen tukemana. Työturvallisuus, työmaan logistiikka, käyttäjäturvallisuus sekä häiriötön opetuksen ja varhaiskasvatuksen toiminta ovat hankkeen keskeisiä onnistumistekijöitä. Urakan tulee olla valmis vaiheittain seuraavasti. Rakennustöiden tulee olla vaiheittain valmiit ja vastaanotettu (sisätilat), sekä rakennusvalvonnan käyttöönottokatselmus vaiheen osalta suoritettu: • Rakennustyöt vaihe 1. (päiväkoti) 22.12.2027 • Rakennustyöt vaihe 2. (koulu, vanha osa) 22.12.2028 • Rakennustyöt vaihe 3. (koulu uusi osa) 1.8.2029 • Koulun keittiön saneeraustyöt tulee tehdä 1.6-15.8 2028 välisenä aikana. Välitavoitteet pihatöiden osalta: • Saattoliikennealue ja päiväkodin leikkipiha valmis ja vastaanotettu 31.7.2027 Kokonaisurakka julkisivu- vesikatto- ja pihatöineen valmis ja vastaanotettu 3.12.2029. Urakan aikataulu voi muuttua tarjouspyynnössä kuvatulla tavalla.

title: Germany – Railway bridge construction work – EÜ-Dahlweg, Brücke und Gleise
description: CargoBeamer ist ein international tätiger Logistikdienstleister mit Sitz in Deutschland und bietet im kombinierten Verkehr innovative Lösungen, um kranbare und nicht kranbare Sattelauflieger umweltfreundlich über die Schiene zu transportieren. Die CargoBeamer Terminal Kaldenkirchen GmbH beabsichtigt den Ersatzneubau der Eisenbahnüberführung EÜ Dahlweg in Nettetal-Kaldenkirchen im Bereich des CargoBeamer-Terminals. Das bestehende Bauwerk befindet sich bei Bahn-km 18,490 der Strecke 2510 Viersen–Kaldenkirchen im Bereich des Ausziehgleises 21 und überführt die Gleisanlage über den Dahlweg. Bei dem Bestandsbauwerk handelt es sich um eine Gewölbebrücke aus Ziegelmauerwerk mit Schrägflügeln. Aufgrund des baulichen Zustands und des Alters ist ein vollständiger Ersatzneubau vorgesehen. Die Vergabe erfolgt als funktionale Generalübernehmerleistung mit Pauschalvergütung. Der Auftragnehmer übernimmt die gemäß den Vergabeunterlagen geschuldeten Planungs-, Genehmigungs-, Untersuchungs-, Koordinierungs-, Rückbau- und Bauleistungen einschließlich der erforderlichen Prüfungen, Dokumentation und Übergabe eines vollständig funktionsfähigen und abnahmefähigen Bauwerks.

title: Pk-yritysbarometrin toteuttaminen vuodelle 2027 (VN/20171/2026)
description: Pk-yritysbarometrin toteuttaminen vuodelle 2027 (VN/20171/2026) Tarjouspyynnön kohde Hankinnan kohteena on pk-yritysten suhdanneodotuksia selvittävän barometrin tiedonkeruun ja raportoinnin toteuttaminen kahdesti vuodessa. Pk-yritysbarometrissa kuvataan pienten ja keski-suurten yritysten toimintaa ja niiden taloudellista toimintaympäristöä. Tarkastelun kohteena ovat pk-yritysten suhdanneodotukset ja niiden kehitys, kasvu ja uudistuminen. Lisäksi käsitellään kansainvälistymistä, investointeja ja rahoitusta. Ensimmäinen barometrin kyselykierros toteutetaan joulu- tammikuussa (julkistaminen helmikuun puolivälissä) ja toinen heinä- elokuussa (julkistaminen syyskuun puoliväliin mennessä) vuonna 2027. Ensimmäinen kysely käynnistyisi siis joulukuussa 2026 ja kyselylomakkeen päivittäminen marraskuussa 2026. Esimerkit kysymyslomakkeesta ovat liitteinä. Kysymyslomakkeen pituus on enintään 50 kysymystä. Kullekin kierrokselle kysymyslomake vahvistetaan kuitenkin aina erikseen. Osa kysymyksistä on vaihtuvia. Lisäksi joitain aihepiirejä tarkastellaan sekä suppealla että laajalla kysymyspatteristolla siten, että osa kysymyksistä sisältyy vain kevään tai syksyn barometriin. Kysely tehdään suomeksi ja ruotsiksi. Lomakkeen käännöstyöstä vastaa tilaaja. Kohdejoukko ja otos Kyselyn kohdejoukkona ovat pk-yritykset (alle 250 henkilöä työllistävät). Otosjoukko muodostetaan siten, että se rakenteeltaan (alueellisuus, toimialajako ja henkilökunnan koko) vastaa mahdollisimman hyvin pk-yritysrakennetta Suomessa. Otantakehikkona on käytetty TOL 2008 toimiala-luokitusta ja Tilastokeskuksen Yritysrekisteriä tai muuta laajapohjaista yritystietokantaa. Toimittajalla tulee olla käytössään yritysten yhteystietojen hankintaan soveltuva kattava rekisteri, jota voidaan tarvittaessa täydentää Suomen Yrittäjien jäsenrekisterin tiedoin. Toimittajan tulee seurata vastaajajoukkoa ja siihen perustuvien tulosten edustavuutta tiedonkeruiden aikana. Toimittajan tulee poimia otokseen ja saada vastaukset riittävältä määrältä yrityksiä siten, että alueellinen, toimialoittainen ja henkilökunnan kokoluokittainen edustavuus toteutuu. Yleensä pk-yritysbarometrin tietopohjana on ollut noin 4 500–6 000 vastanneen yrityksen tiedot. Kysely toteutetaan pääasiassa internetkyselynä, jota voidaan täydentää mobiilipohjaisella kyselyllä. Tasapainoinen näyte varmistetaan tarvittaessa lisähaastatteluilla puhelimitse. kts. tarkemmin liite 1 Hankinnan kuvaus,

title: Mechanical Maintenance Services – RCMP Arviat and Cambridge Bay, NU
description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Arviat and Cambridge Bay, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for the Supply and Delivery of Mechanical Maintenance Services at the RCMP Arviat Detachment and Cambridge Bay Detachment. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). Policy on Reciprocal Procurement This solicitation of bids is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 12-months from the date of contract. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, technical merit and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, 30 % for the technical merit and 40% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Integrity Regime administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. For more information and to review eligibility criteria and register, visit: www.canada.ca/indigenousbusinessdirectory.

description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE, NOT A REQUEST FOR A QUOTE (RFQ). A RFQ WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. title: Hydrogen Generator for Gas Chromatography
description: The United States Embassy seeks qualified and authorized reseller of one (1) on demand laboratory hydrogen generator, plus installation, gas distribution, commissioning, training and warranty services, as described below: PEAK SCIENTIFIC INTURA H2 250 HYDROGEN GENERATOR (AUTO-FILL), WITH MANUFACTURER'S STANDARD WARRANTY QUANTITY: 1 Peak Scientific part number: 3305698-0-02 (auto-fill) Flow rate up to 250 cc/min; 99.99999% purity; output pressure up to 175 psi Standard warranty: 12-month comprehensive warranty and 36-month PEM cell warranty both starting at Government acceptance Operator's manual and warranty certificate in English PEAK INTURA H2 ANNUAL SERVICE KIT QUANTITY: 1 Peak Scientific part number: 3306178 ON-SITE INSTALLATION, GAS DISTRIBUTION, COMMISSIONING AND TRAINING QUANTITY: 1 Firm-fixed price. No extra labor-hour charges. Performed at IFSLM, Kingston, Jamaica, by Peak-certified technicians, in English. Supply and install all clean, GC-grade tubing, fittings, tees/manifolds and point-of-use regulators to deliver hydrogen to the Agilent 7890A GC/5975C VL MSD and the Agilent 7890A GC-FID, which sit next to each other. Connect the generator to the lab's existing DI water supply for auto-fill. Leak-test every connection. Show that each instrument works on generator-supplied hydrogen, including the switch from helium to hydrogen carrier gas on the 5975C system. Provide one (1) day of on-site operator training for approximately ten (10) IFSLM staff, covering operation, routine maintenance, water quality requirements and hydrogen safety, including safe hydrogen use in the GC oven and MSD. Provide an installation and commissioning report. 004 � SHIPPING TO KINGSTON, JAMAICA QUANTITY: 1 FOB Destination: U.S. Embassy Kingston, 142 Old Hope Road Kingston 6 Jamaica, including all customs, brokerage, insurance and freight charges for the items to be delivered door to door (DTP). title: Electrical and Electronic Properties Measuring and Testing Instruments
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION: The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) intends to procure a commercial Radio Frequency (RF) record and playback solution. The acquisition consists of: One (1) Rohde & Schwarz (R&S) IQW Wideband I/Q Recorder One (1) R&S SMW200A Vector Signal Generator Associated software, licenses (including the FSW-B517 digital streaming interface upgrade), cables, and support. The required solution must be capable of playing back previously recorded RF signals from a Government-owned library stored in a proprietary R&S In-phase Quadrature (I/Q) format. The system must stream the high-speed I/Q data and convert it back to the analog RF data needed to stimulate the EA-18G aircraft's electronic warfare systems in a laboratory test environment. SOLE-SOURCE RATIONALE: The Government has determined that Rohde & Schwarz is the only source capable of satisfying this requirement. This determination is based on the following: 1. Proprietary Data Compatibility: The EA-18G program's critical test data library, which consists of terabytes of classified threat recordings, exists exclusively in a proprietary Rohde & Schwarz I/Q data format. The Government�s existing I/Q data library is maintained in proprietary R&S format. The required solution must use those files natively or otherwise demonstrate preservation of data integrity, metadata, timing, sample rate, bandwidth, phase coherence, and signal fidelity without introducing unacceptable schedule risk. Market research did not identify an available non-R&S solution that met those conditions. 2. Unacceptable Schedule Risk and Cost: As determined by market research (Sources Sought N6893627Q5001), The alternate OEM solutions evaluated by the technical activity relied on file translation, conversion, or non-native interface approaches that would require validation of converted I/Q data and present unacceptable data-fidelity and schedule risk. WesTest proposed an R&S-supported integration approach intended to avoid or control conversion; however, WesTest subsequently withdrew because it could not assure the required OEM-backed proprietary support. The Government�s existing I/Q data library requires native use of proprietary R&S-format files. Market research did not identify an available source, other than Rohde & Schwarz, that could furnish the complete required configuration including the proprietary equipment, upgrades, licenses, and OEM-backed technical support without data conversion or unacceptable technical and schedule risk. Response Instructions Responses are are due no later than 15 days After posting Submit responses by e-mail to: Primary Point of Contact: Stephanie Amoni, stephanie.j.amoni.civ@us.navy.mil, 564-230-3333 Secondary Point of Contact: Joyce Toye, joyce.n.toye2.civ@us.navy.mil, 858-978-4847 Use the following e-mail subject line: Response to Notice of Intent to Sole Source � N6893627Q5001� I/Q Test Equipment Capability Disclaimer: Information received will be used solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of a response. Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at https://sam.gov/.

title: Purina Dog Food RFI/Sources Sought
description: After reviewing this Request for Information, interested vendors are requested to submit responses by November 13, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. ET to the points of contact below. This is a Request for Information/Sources Sought Notice issued by the General Services Administration to gather information from prospective vendors interested in providing Purina dog food and related products in support of the National Stock Number Program and dog requirements. This is not a solicitation, request for quote, or request for proposal. The Government is conducting market research to determine vendor capability, interest, commercial practices, pricing structures, and recommended terms for a potential follow-on requirement. The Government is considering a firm-fixed-price five-year indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity contract with one base year and four one-year option periods. Pricing for the base year and all option years would be submitted and evaluated at time of award. The Government is also considering a lowest price technically acceptable evaluation approach with price and technical factors. The specific acquisition strategy, evaluation factors, and terms and conditions will be identified in any future solicitation. NAICS Code 311111, Dog and Cat Food Manufacturing, applies to this RFI. Vendors interested in this potential requirement are encouraged to ensure their System for Award Management registration is active and includes the applicable NAICS code. Vendors are encouraged to register or update their SAM.gov record at https://www.sam.gov at this time. The Government may use responses to this RFI to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether any small business or socioeconomic set aside may be appropriate. All interested firms are invited to submit a response. The draft product list includes 27 brand name Purina products identified by the military veterinarian to cover a range of military working dog dietary needs. The Government only intends to include products approved by the military veterinarian. Based on current ordering history, and assuming outside the continental United States requirements are removed from the follow on contract, the Government estimates annual continental United States (CONUS) demand of approximately 5,500 bags of dog food. This estimate is based on ordering activity from extrapolating the most recent six months and may be refined as additional customer input is received. The Government is still assessing potential additional military demand, which is not included in this estimate. The Government anticipates that orders would be issued for direct delivery to ordering agencies. The Government is also considering requiring vendors to provide tracking and order status updates through a Government vendor portal. The information provided in this notice is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Government will not reimburse vendors for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response to this notice. Requested Vendor Feedback Interested vendors are requested to provide brief responses to the following: Are you interested in this potential requirement, and can you provide all products on the attached Purina Food Plan list? If not, please identify which listed products you can and cannot provide. Some of these products require veterinary authorization/prescriptions. Can you fulfill orders for veterinary diet products that require authorization? Are any listed products unavailable, difficult to obtain, or subject to supply issues? What pricing structure would help keep prices low and competitive for this requirement? For example, tiered pricing, minimum order amounts, or another commercial pricing structure. Are you capable of providing MIL-STD-129R labeling, if required? If so, would this requirement affect pricing, lead time, or your interest in the requirement? What delivery timeframe would be commercially reasonable for CONUS orders? If awarded, would your company be willing to request access to the Government vendor portal and provide tracking and order status updates through that system? Response Information Please include the following in your response: Company name; Point of contact; Email and phone number; Unique Entity ID, if available; SAM.gov registration status; Business size and socioeconomic status, if applicable; Whether your company is an authorized distributor, reseller, or supplier of Purina products; and Brief responses to the questions above. Responses are requested by November 13, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. ET to Stephanie Bridgewater at stephanie.bridgewater@gsa.gov and Tracy Harper at tracy.harper@gsa.gov. Attachment 1: Purina Food Plan

title: C1DA--PROJECT 528A5-27-503 A/E Design Replace Flat Roofs Canandaigua VAMC
description: Sources Sought Notice THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY NOR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking a qualified Architect-Engineering (AE) firm to provide Schematics, Design Development, Construction Documents, Technical Specifications, Construction Period Services, Site Visits, Cost Estimates, As-Built Documentation, and all other related information for Project 58A5-27-503 Project Design Replace Flat Roof at the Canandaigua VA Medical Center, 400 Fort Hill Avenue, Canandaigua, NY 14424. this project is to develop a conditions-report and design documents for replacing the existing flat roofs on buildings 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 36, 37, 118, and various connecting tunnels. The conditions report shall be prepared after a thorough investigation of the existing conditions with estimated costs and improvements. The following design will include all selected repairs and improvements from the conditions report that fit within VA construction budget. As part of the report and design effort, the existing conditions shall be tested and verified, including evaluation of the drainage, materiality, masonry, fall protection, equipment, ACM, insulation, and structural integrity. New work may include redesign / reconstruction of support structures, drainage, roof type change, and parapet wall restoration to ensure water intrusion and legacy issues are mitigated. In addition to repairs and modifications, all interior drainage piping shall be replaced minimum 10 from roof drain unless, otherwise discussed with VA for convenience or practical reasons or as needed due to conditions of ease or degradation. This requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act as implemented in FAR Subpart 36.6. Applicable NAICS code is 541330 and small business size standard of $25.5 Million. Magnitude of Construction is between $500,000 and $1,000,000. This is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Set Aside. The anticipated award date of the proposed A-E Contract is on or before December 30, 2026. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov ) and are visible/verified/certified as SDVOSB in Dynamic Small Business Search (https://dsbs.sba.gov/search/dsp_dsbs.cfm) at time of submission of their qualifications in order to be considered for an award. In order to assure compliance with VAAR clauses, 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (NOV 2022) and 852.219-73 VA Notice to Total Set-Aside for Verified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (NOV 2022), all firms submitting a SF 330 for this notice are required to indicate what percentage of the cost of contract performance will be expended on the concerns employees and in which discipline(s) and percentage of cost of contract performance to be expended (and in what disciplines) by any other consultant/subcontractor or otherwise used small or large business entity(s). Any consultant/subcontractor or otherwise business entity(s) used must be identified by name, office location and size/type of business (i.e., SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), small, large, etc.). Failure to provide this information will deem the firm s SF 330 submittal as non-responsive and preclude further evaluation All A/E firms are advised that in accordance with VAAR 836.606-71 the total cost of the production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings and specifications shall not exceed six (6) percent of the estimate cost of construction. Other A-E fees are not included in the six (6) percent. Additionally, FAR Clause 52.236-22 (c) - Design Within Funding Limitation, will be applicable to this procurement action. SCOPE OF SERVICE REQUIRED Project no. 528A5-27-503: A/E Design Replace Flat Roof LOCATION Canandaigua VAMC, 400 Fort Hill Avenue Canandaigua, NY 14424 COST RANGE Magnitude of Construction is between $500,000.00 and $1,000,000.00 Estimated Construction Cost Range: $5,000,000. TYPE OF CONTRACT CONTEMPLATED The Department of Veterans Affairs is contemplating awarding a firm fixed price contract. DESIGN COMPLETION PERIOD: The Department of Veterans Affairs requires design and contract support services. The A/E shall deliver 100% bid documents in 255 calendar days from the Notice to Proceed (NTP). SELECTION CRITERIA DESCRIPTIONS The submitted SF-330s will be evaluated on the following criteria: This acquisition will be in accordance with FAR Part 36.602-1 and VAAR Part 836.602-1. The following evaluation criteria will be used to evaluate SF-330 technical proposals: The A/E must demonstrate its qualifications with respect to the published evaluation criteria for all services. Evaluation Criteria is of equal importance with an exception of criterion 1 and 7 which shall carry an additional weight multiplier of 1.5. Each criterion shall be rated out of a score of 1 to 10. Total possible score is 80. Specific evaluation criteria include: 1.Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, roof replacements, structural repairs, drainage, temporary systems and investigative services. 2. Professional Qualifications necessary for performance of site surveys such as the one described within the SOW including qualified personnel and approach to this scope. 3. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time. 4. Past Performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules. 5. Specific experience and qualifications of personnel proposed for assignment to the project and their record of working together as a team. 6. Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualified firms, given the nature and size of the project. 7. Specific examples of survey documents as described in the scope of work and approach to preparation of the documents as requested by the VA. 8. Record of significant claims against the firm because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services. Criterion 1 - Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, roof replacements, structural repairs, drainage, temporary systems and investigative services. Offerors will be evaluated on specialized experience and technical competence in the performance of services similar to those anticipated under this contract with regard to: Experience with roofing systems. Experience with design of building drainage systems. Experience with specialized HVAC and electrical design for healthcare facilities. Experience in providing post construction award services (shop drawing review, as-built drawing and Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) preparation, construction inspection services, and Operating and Maintenance Manuals). Experience with government designs and construction. Experience with historic buildings, preservation, and alterations. Submission requirements: Provide a detailed write-up of how the firm has accomplished the requirement. In addition, provide up to five (5) projects completed or substantially completed within the past five (5) years that best illustrate specialized experience of the proposed team in the areas outlined above. title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and planning services – BIM-Planungsleistung - ZKB 2030 - Friedrichshafen Flughafen und Meckenbeuren
description: Gegenstand der Vergabe sind BIM-Planungsleistungen (Einfach BIM) für die Erneuerung der Verkehrsstationen Friedrichshafen Flughafen und Meckenbeuren an der Strecke 4500. Die Planung erfolgt als Einphasenplanung für die Leistungsphasen 1 bis 7 gemäß HOAI unter Anwendung der BIM-Methodik. An beiden Haltepunkten sind jeweils die zwei vorhandenen Bahnsteige zu erneuern. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere die Erneuerung der Bahnsteigbeläge, die Erneuerung der Bahnsteigkanten, die Erneuerung der Beleuchtungsanlagen sowie den Austausch der Ausstattungselemente. Am Haltepunkt Meckenbeuren ist zusätzlich die Erneuerung des Stufenbelags der Personenunterführung vorgesehen. Projektstandorte: Friedrichshafen Flughafen (Bahnhofs-Nr. 5987) Strecke 4500, km 193,0 bis km 193,3 Meckenbeuren (Bahnhofs-Nr. 4015) Strecke 4500, km 188,7 bis km 189,0 Ziel des Projekts ist die Modernisierung der Bahnsteiganlagen zur Verbesserung der Verkehrssicherheit, Funktionalität und Aufenthaltsqualität unter Anwendung der BIM-Methodik. Folgende Leistungsbilder sind Bestandteil der Vergabe: - Objektplanung Verkehrsanlagen gemäß HOAI - Fachplanung 50-Hz-Anlagen einschließlich Bahnsteigbeleuchtung - Objekt- und Tragwerksplanung Ingenieurbauwerke für die Erneuerung der Treppenanlagen bzw. Treppenbeläge - Baugrunduntersuchungen einschließlich Baugrundgutachten - Erstellung eines BIM-Grundlagenmodells auf Basis der bereitgestellten Vermessungsdaten Die Planung ist unter Berücksichtigung der bahnbetrieblichen Randbedingungen, der Anforderungen an die Barrierefreiheit sowie der gültigen Regelwerke der DB InfraGO AG durchzuführen.

title: Balfour Beatty - Roads North of the Thames - LTC - Bridge Bearings
description: The Lower Thames Crossing Roads North Programme is seeking expressions of interest from organisations with experience in the design support, manufacture, supply and installation of bridge bearings for major highway and infrastructure projects. The scope comprises the provision of specialist bridge bearing product and methodology support to our Design Partner during the development of the detailed design, followed by the manufacture, supply, delivery and installation of bridge bearings to 16 structures across the Lower Thames Crossing Roads North project. As part of our procurement planning, we are seeking to better understand market capability, capacity and preferred delivery models to help inform the final procurement strategy and packaging approach. Through this PQQ, we are looking to engage with experienced suppliers who can provide innovative, durable and cost-effective bridge bearing solutions whilst supporting collaborative design development and safe, efficient installation. What We're Looking For We would like to hear from organisations with experience in one or more of the following: Proven experience in the design support, manufacture and installation of bridge bearings for major highway and infrastructure projects. Experience of working collaboratively with design consultants and principal contractors during detailed design development. Appropriate quality management systems. Relevant health, safety and environmental accreditations. Capability to manufacture and deliver products to programme requirements. Resources and expertise to undertake installation activities safely and efficiently. Experience of working within National Highways or similar major infrastructure environments is desirable. We welcome responses from organisations of all sizes, including SMEs, either independently or as part of a consortium, joint venture or wider supply chain arrangement. How to Apply If you are interested in this opportunity, please complete the attached Bridge Bearings Package Eligibility Criteria Questionnaire and return it to the Supply Chain Team by 13.11.26 at: BBLTCProcurementandSupplyChain@balfourbeatty.com Please ensure all sections of the questionnaire are completed, as this will help us gain a full understanding of your organisation's capability, capacity and relevant experience. The qualification questions have been designed to assess your ability to meet Balfour Beatty and Lower Thames Crossing supply chain requirements and will help inform the final procurement strategy for these works. We are particularly interested in understanding your experience in providing technical support during design development, your manufacturing and installation capabilities, available capacity, and your preferred delivery model for supporting major infrastructure projects. Additional information: The Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) is a new road to better connect Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive a change in how we deliver - connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, leaving a skills legacy for the local community and construction industry, all whilst restoring nature and drawing a new blueprint for low-carbon construction. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road, and to do the right thing for local communities and the environment. We can only achieve this with the support of our supply chain, and it is therefore critical that for any supplier to be successful in winning work on LTC, they must demonstrate commitments to supporting delivery of our ambitions: • Delivering the works through a 'zero emissions' solution, and not using diesel on site in any plant or machinery. • Supporting us to leave a skills legacy for the local community, by not only recruiting locally, but upskilling your workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher paid higher skilled work. • Helping to facilitate successful opportunities by providing early careers roles, as well as inspiring young people into construction through delivery of STEM engagement.

title: Tobyhanna Gates & Turnstiles
description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

title: RFI Comprehensive Medical Review & Audit Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 to conduct market research. The Government's purpose is planning only; this notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP)/Request for Quotation (RFQ) nor a promise to issue one in the future. The Government will not pay any costs for responding, and any submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. The Government is not seeking proposals or quotes at this time. Scope of Interest / Functional Areas: The Government is assessing the market�s capability to provide comprehensive support under the following disciplines: a. Audits for Medicare Parts A, B, D, and Medicaid medical record review and consultative services b. Audits for Medicare Part C medical record review and consultative services c. Evaluations and Inspections medical record review and consultative services d. Expert consultant and witness services in support of the Office of Investigations and/or Office of Counsel to the Inspector General A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is provided for industry feedback; requirements may change prior to any future solicitation. Requested Information (do not submit proposals or quotes): Please provide high level, non price specific information addressing the elements below. Do not include proprietary pricing, line item estimates, or any proposal/quote content. Section 1: Corporate Capability & Experience a. PWS Alignment: Demonstrate your organization's core capability to fulfill the functional areas outlined in the draft PWS. b. Medical Review Experience: Outline your firm's high-level experience in conducting large-volume medical claims reviews for audits and evaluations and inspections; and support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses specifically across the following five domains (as referenced in the attached PWS): 1. Audit Medicare Parts A/B/D and Medicaid 2. Audit Medicare Part C 3. Evaluations and Inspections 4. Office of Investigations 5. Office of Counsel to the Inspector General c. Geographic Reach: Describe your prior experience managing and executing nationwide or multi-jurisdictional medical claim reviews. d. Capacity & Scalability: State your organization's maximum monthly claim review capacity, including your approach to scaling operations between normal workloads and surge conditions. e Teaming & Subcontracting: Identify potential subcontracting partners or specialized vendors you would anticipate utilizing, including an estimated percentage breakdown of work performed by the prime contractor versus subcontractors. Section 2: High-Level Technical Approach & Operations a. High-Level Technical Methodology: Describe your conceptual approach to fulfilling the core tasks in PWS. Please limit this narrative to no more than 5 pages total, organized by the 5 PWS sections. Focus on your overarching claims review methodology, general sampling plan frameworks, documentation standards, and typical project timelines rather than a granular, step-by-step solution. b. Quality & Accuracy Frameworks: Outline your corporate quality assurance processes, internal review protocols, and standard strategies used to reduce error rates and ensure consistency across large volumes. b. Staffing & Key Qualifications: Provide a conceptual staffing structure or organizational chart. Identify the typical roles, credentials (e.g., MD, RN, CPC), and qualifications of the key personnel required to successfully support a PWS of this nature. Please identify whether these staff will need to be hired or if they are current employees/contractors. Also, indicate staffing availability for physicians with specialties (i.e. hospice, vascular surgeon, nephrologist, physical medicine and rehabilitation or physiatrists). c. Risk & Mitigation: Identify the primary technical or operational challenges anticipated with a medical review scope of this size and outline your high-level mitigation strategies. Section 3: Past Performance & Market Pricing a. Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar Federal medical review contracts performed within the last five years. Also, provide up to three examples of similar Federal support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses within the last five years. b. Performance Outcomes: Summarize the high-level outcomes of those past contracts, focusing on standard metrics such as timeliness, accuracy rates (including rate at which findings were overturned during the appeals process), and a history of successful audit findings. c. Cost Drivers & Efficiencies: Provide a general overview of your commercial pricing structure and the primary cost drivers (e.g., specific labor categories, specialized technology/AI tools, administrative overhead). Highlight any built-in efficiencies or innovative workflows in your approach that typically yield cost savings for the government. Section 4: Industry Feedback & PWS Refinement a. Clarity & Feasibility Review: Identify any requirements, metrics, or tasks within the draft PWS that appear ambiguous, overly restrictive, or technologically infeasible based on current commercial market capabilities. b. Recommendations for Improvement: Suggest specific enhancements, industry standard metrics, or structural changes to the PWS that would improve the clarity, feasibility, and competitiveness of the final solicitation. Submission Instructions: Email responses by November 13, 2026, 12:00 PM Eastern Time to the Points of Contact below. Mark proprietary information clearly; the Government may use non proprietary information to refine its acquisition approach. Points of Contact: a. Contracting Officer: Shavonda Jamison � Shavonda_Jamison@ibc.doi.gov b. Contracting Specialist: Dorothy Royster � Dorothy_Royster@ibc.doi.gov Attachments: a. Draft PWS (for market research and feedback only; subject to change). Disclaimer: This RFI is for market research; it does not commit the Government to any acquisition. The Government will not reimburse costs for responding. Not responding does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. No proposals or quotes will be accepted in response to this notice.

title: MDC BROOKLYN - REMOVE AND REPLACE SHOWER PARTITIONS
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial construction for MDC Brooklyn located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY, 11232, and is prepared in accordance with the format in subpart FAR Revision Subpart 12.202(b)(1), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes as the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation is issued (see attached). You are required to provide all pages of the written attached solicitation with your complete quotation. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) anticipates issuance of solicitation 15BBR027Q00000003 for the award of a firm fixed-price construction contract titled REMOVE AND REPLACE SHOWER PARTITIONS at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, NY. MDC Brooklyn is a federal correctional facility located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY 11232. The contractor is responsible to provide all equipment and labor to remove and replace all existing shower partitions (with attached changing rooms) and bathroom stall partitions on the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 6th floors of the East Building at MDC Brooklyn. Each floor contains a North and South side, and each side includes: 6-bathroom stalls 7- shower stalls with changing rooms Changing rooms shall be 39.5 inches deep and include a door All partitions shall be floor- and overhead braced. Materials and finishes shall include: Powder-coated steel partitions 58-inch doors and panels Chrome zamac hardware Silver Vein color for all doors and panels Contractor shall also remove and replace all affected existing restroom accessories including, but not limited to, handicap grab bars, toilet paper holders, sanitary napkin dispenser, towel bars, soap dispensers, etc. Contractor to provide industrial standard labor and materials warranties from date of substantial completion. See the Statement of Work (SOW) attachment. The performance period for the project will be 60 calendar days from issuance of the notice to proceed. The timeframe allotted will allow adequate time for security clearances to be obtained, materials to be ordered and delivered on site, the removal of the old equipment, the work to be completed, system testing to be completed, and demobilization from the work site. Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation 36.204, the estimated magnitude of the project lies between $100,000 and $250,000. (NOTE: This range is one of 8 available ranges from FAR 36.204 and is not meant to imply that the project has necessarily been estimated/budgeted to the maximum of the selected range. It merely conveys that the estimate/budget lies somewhere within that range.) Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. title: LLA Navigation Lock Switchgear
description: Title: LLA Navigation Lock Switchgear Replacement: The work is located at the Lower Granite Dam, Pomeroy, Washington. The solicitation will be issued as a Best Value Trade-Off (BVTO) Request for Proposal (RFP) and result in a single firm-fixed price construction contract. This procurement is a small business set aside. 100% Performance and payment bonds will be required for this project. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS code for this project is 238210 Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors and the associated small business size standard is $19 million. Solicitation number W912EF27RA002 will be posted to the SAM.gov Contract Opportunities website on or about mid November 2026. The proposal due date will be contained in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments that may be issued. The solicitation will be made available for download on the SAM.gov Contract Opportunities website. Offerors are responsible for checking the referenced page for any updates to the Notice. The Government is not responsible for any loss of Internet connectivity or for an offeror's inability to access the documents posted at the referenced website. Proposals will be due approximately 30 days after the solicitation is posted. The exact proposal due date will be indicated in the solicitation. System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors must register in the SAM at https://sam.gov/content/home prior to receiving an award. NOTE: The response date that is required to post this notice is not in any way a due date for any submission. This is a pre-solicitation notice only. Scope: The scope of the work involves replacing existing medium and low voltage switchgear lineups and their associated feeder cables with modernized medium and low voltage switchgear and motor control center lineups at Lower Granite Dam Navigation Lock. The main features of work includes: Provide and install one (1) new medium voltage switch gear. Provide and install one (1) new low voltage switch gear. Provide and install two (2) new motor control center lineups. Provide modernized controls for existing electrical loads. Provide one (1) new 4,160/480-V 1,000 kVA transformer. Provide lighting load centers to replace existing panels. Provide new concrete housekeeping pads for new electrical equipment. Provide new cable trays and conduits where required by circuit reconfigurations and to bring fill ratios to levels that meet electrical codes. Provide an HMI screen to replace an existing annunciator panel. Demolish existing medium and low voltage switchgear, motor controls centers, and transformers. Demolish the existing 480VAC feeders routed from existing low voltage switchgear and motor control centers. Seal hatch and any expansion joints, or cracks, to prevent water intrusion in an existing electrical room. This work is anticipated to be performed in 2028 and 2029, with cutover power construction work being completed during the 2028 and 2029 navigation lock outages. Access to the navigation lock deck and electrical substation rooms will be available for workers and equipment. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THE SOLICITATION EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER THE CLOSING DATE. title: Request for Information (RFI): Verification and Compliance Checking for Natural-Language Network Requirements (FastVacc)
description: Modern networks need to be reconfigured quickly in response to mission changes or emerging threats, but checking compliance with security requirements can take months. This creates a window in which adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities introduced by those changes. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Information Processing Techniques Office (IPTO) seeks information on approaches, tools and practices for closing that window by reducing, by 2-3 orders of magnitude, the time and cost of verifiable compliance checking. DARPA envisions a capability that would take as input two items: (a) a requirements document written in natural language and (b) the configurations in a concrete network. In an offline phase, it would reason about the requirements for inconsistency, redundancy and incompleteness, and output consistent, non-redundant and completed requirements. Then, it would check, in near real-time, whether the concrete configurations satisfy all of the requirements. In all cases, its output would be understandable by a human.

title: LLA Navigation Lock Switchgear
description: Title: LLA Navigation Lock Switchgear Replacement: The work is located at the Lower Granite Dam, Pomeroy, Washington. Scope: The scope of the work involves replacing existing medium and low voltage switchgear lineups and their associated feeder cables with modernized medium and low voltage switchgear and motor control center lineups at Lower Granite Dam Navigation Lock. The main features of work includes: Provide and install one (1) new medium voltage switch gear. Provide and install one (1) new low voltage switch gear. Provide and install two (2) new motor control center lineups. Provide modernized controls for existing electrical loads. Provide one (1) new 4,160/480-V 1,000 kVA transformer. Provide lighting load centers to replace existing panels. Provide new concrete housekeeping pads for new electrical equipment. Provide new cable trays and conduits where required by circuit reconfigurations and to bring fill ratios to levels that meet electrical codes. Provide an HMI screen to replace an existing annunciator panel. Demolish existing medium and low voltage switchgear, motor controls centers, and transformers. Demolish the existing 480VAC feeders routed from existing low voltage switchgear and motor control centers. Seal hatch and any expansion joints, or cracks, to prevent water intrusion in an existing electrical room. This work is anticipated to be performed in 2028 and 2029, with cutover power construction work being completed during the 2028 and 2029 navigation lock outages. Access to the navigation lock deck and electrical substation rooms will be available for workers and equipment. A CQC System Manager employed by the prime contractor is required to be on-site for each shift of the Contractor's operations. The CQC System Manager must possess a minimum of 5 years relevant experience in a supervisory or management position such as Quality Control Manager, Quality Assurance Manager, or Construction Manager directly involved in the management of construction quality at the project site. In addition, the CQC System Manager shall have completed the course entitled �Construction Quality Management for Contractors� within the last 5 years. title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 27 October 2026: P00002 Updated PWS dated 27 October 2026. Post Round 1-3 Q&A's. 23 October 2026: P00001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 722310, Food Service Contractors, which has a size standard of $47 million. This requirement was previously announced, but never solicited, under ID: HT940826RE017. The Government has updated some of the documents that were previously posted as a result of questions asked since the initial posting; if an interested party still has questions or feels that any information is still unclear, they are encouraged to submit those questions to the POCs listed herein. The Defense Health Agency has a requirement for non-personal services providing qualified labor and management necessary to perform nutrition care food management, supervisory, technical, administrative, and clerical services that focus primarily on the following areas: dining facility management functions, therapeutic food preparation, patient tray assembly and delivery service, clinical training, facility sanitation, janitorial duties as it relates to the services being provided, and the associated logistics analysis and management functions in support of the Nutrition Care Divisions for five (5) Military Medical Treatment Facilities (MTFs). The following MTFs requiring the Nutrition Care Food Service support are: Weed Army Community Hospital (Fort Irwin, California), General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri), Irwin Army Community Hospital (Fort Riley, Kansas), Winn Army Community Hospital (Fort Stewart, Georgia), and Keller Army Community Hospital (West Point, New York). A transition period of 1 December 2026 � 31 January 2027, base period of 1 February 2027 � 30 September 2027, and two (2) twelve-month option periods through 30 September 2029 are contemplated. The contract will be firm-fixed-price, with a set monthly price established per MTF. Multiple contracts may be awarded, up to one (1) per MTF. The Randolph Sheppard Act (RSA) applies to this requirement; therefore, priority will be given to any responsive State Licensing Agency (SLA) pursuant to the RSA. The priority established by the RSA applies to the award of contracts for the operation of cafeterias on Federal property. NOTE: The evaluation criteria will be the same for all offerors, including any responsible SLA. However, the solicitation will be issued on a full-and-open basis with a small business participation (eg, subcontracting) plan as one of the evaluation criteria for other-than-small businesses and non-SLAs. The solicitation will be issued on or about 16 October 2026, with an estimated closing date of 4 November 2026. Questions are due via email to the POCs listed below by 22 October 2026. title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: 23 October 2026: P00001 Extend the due date to 13 November 2026. **Please take note that the solicitation number has been updated to HTC71127QE127 due to overlap in Fiscal Years** The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: Corrective and Preventative Maintenance of Electronic Security Systems at the Ronald Reagan Building
description: RFQ Amendment 0005 has been posted below. Furthermore, industry questions and answers are forthcoming based on the questions received from industry. RFQ Amendment 0004 has been posted below. RFQ Amendment 0003 has been posted below. RFQ Amendment 0002 has been posted below. RFQ Amendment 0001 has been posted below. NOTE: PLEASE BE ADVISED BEGINNING MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 TRAVEL RESTIRICTIONS BEGIN AROUND THE RONALD REGAN BUILDING DUE TO THE PREPARATION FOR THE GRAND PRIX RACE. PLEASE ACCOUNT FOR POTENTIAL TRAVEL DELAY AND ALLOW ADDITONAL TRAVEL TIME TO ATTEND THE SITE VISIT SCHEDULED FOR MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 AT 10AM ET. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Protective Service (FPS) has a requirement for corrective and preventative maintenance of electronic security systems and the replacement and removal of outdated electronic security systems at the Ronald Reagan Building (DC0459). The Contractor shall provide preventive maintenance, repair, replacement, lifecycle upgrades and installations to meet assessed security vulnerabilities / gaps in existing security systems. The services include, but are not limited to, routine and preventive maintenance, repairs and service calls. The VSS equipment includes, interior and exterior fixed IP cameras, controllers, monitors and NVR recorders, power supplies, and all associated ancillary equipment and infrastructure that are part of the Ronald Reagan Building Complex. The Period of Performance is for a one-year base ordering period with four one-year optional ordering periods. An Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with fixed priced provisions is anticipated. This acquisition is being solicited as a total Women-Owned Small Business set aside. Resultant task orders under this contract will be firm fixed price. The source selection process to be utilized for this acquisition is best value/trade-off. The technical, non-price factor, when combined, is more important than price. The submission requirements and evaluation criteria will be defined in the solicitation. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561621 with size standard is $25 million. The successful Contractor is required to be register with the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for award. All questions must be submitted in writing to Contract Specialist Christopher Kelly at Christopher.Kelly@fps.dhs.gov.

title: Cost Per Reportable Result Purchase of Immunohistochemistry Reagents for Laboratory Tests.
description: The VA Puget Sound Health Care System Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Service requires a histology staining workflow system which includes: Two (2) immunohistochemistry (IHC) and two (2) in-situ hybridization (ISH) immunostainers, and two (2) special stainers, and a specimen tracking system which promotes proper identification of specimens and slides and will audit workflow to identify areas that need improvement and reduce errors. The tracking system will improve patient safety, provide a chain of custody, and will monitor productivity. All the components of the workflow system must communicate with each other in order to track the workflow. The stainers attached to this system must be automated and allow the system to track and label slides for special staining and immunostaining. The workflow system must be compatible with the IT systems VISTA and/or Cerner, as well as any other new electronic health record system the VA acquires and also be compatible with Data Innovations middleware.

title: Quality Assurance Services - Civil Works, Interagency and International Services (IIS), and Military Construction Projects in Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to award an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) for Quality Assurance Services across Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. This procurement follows the presolicitation notice previously synopsized under solicitation number W51DQV26RA007. The contractor shall provide comprehensive quality assurance oversight supporting Civil Works, International and Interagency Services (IIS), and Military Construction (MILCON) projects, including navigation, flood risk management, coastal protection, environmental restoration, water resources, and military or federal installations. Services encompass monitoring contractor compliance with plans and specifications, reviewing engineering submittals and technical reports, conducting on-site field inspections of dams, levees, berms, cutoff walls, pump stations, flood control gates, and electrical systems, and performing certified sampling and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, and water. Contract personnel shall also perform daily safety monitoring and prepare daily quality assurance inspection reports. This action is a total small business set-aside under NAICS code 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) with an applicable small business size standard of $19.5 million. The contract ordering period comprises a one-year base period, four 12-month option periods, and one six-month option period, not to exceed a total duration of five years and six months, with a maximum program capacity of $35 million across the contract life.

title: E-Waste Collection Events
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified recyclers capable of organizing residential electronic waste (e-waste) collection events in states without e-waste recycling regulation (i.e., nonregulated states) to support INL�s research and operational mission. This service is essential for raising awareness, increasing collection volumes and verifying whether successful collection methods from a regulated state can be applied to a nonregulated state with comparable results. Eligible states for this work include Alabama, Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Idaho (except eastern and southeastern region), Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Tennessee and Wyoming. BACKGROUND BEA is the Management and Operating Contractor for the DOE located at INL. INL is a DOE national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security and advanced energy innovation. A BEA research team has the lead role on the DOE project titled, �Comparing Strategies to Collect Battery-Containing Devices in States with and without Electronics Recycling Laws.� The proposed service will operate to support this project through Sept. 30, 2027. In the first two years of this project, project teams organized collection events in New York and Idaho. New York is as urban area with established e-waste regulations, and Idaho is a rural area without such requirements. By applying successful collection methods from New York to southeastern Idaho, we observed similar success across 20 e-waste collection events. To further validate these results, we are seeking opportunities to apply our methods in other nonregulated states by organizing six to nine e-waste collection events. SCOPE OF WORK Responding organizations must be capable of delivering the following services: Provide existing status; compile data from existing residential collection activities related to seasonal trends, locations and e-waste types. Organize collection events at new locations in nonregulated states, with each participating organization conducting at least two to three collection events before September 2027. Arrange advertisements on multiple channels to broadcast new collection events and raise awareness about battery-containing e-waste recycling. Provide collection event data including number of participants and quantities of collected e-waste by type PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an EOI that includes the following: Organization information: Organization name, address, organization type, scope of operations, number of employees and primary point of contact. Existing e-waste collection access: Describe existing e-waste collection events, permanent drop-off locations or other collection options available in the proposed service area. Program interest and expected outcomes: Explain why your organization wants to participate in this project and what outcomes you expect to achieve. Service area and target participants: Identify the cities, counties, or communities that will be served by the proposed e-waste collection activities. Community need: Describe the primary e-waste management challenges or unmet needs in the proposed service area. Collection plan: Describe the proposed e-waste collection activities for the program year (by Sept. 1, 2027). Provide the anticipated number of collection events and proposed cities, counties, or collection locations. Provide communication strategies (i.e. social media, mail, news, flyers, etc.) to raise awareness and promote collection events. Downstream e-waste management: Identify who will transport, receive, recycle, process, or otherwise manage the collected e-waste. Recycler/processor qualifications: Identify relevant certifications or qualifications of the entities handling collected e-waste, such as R2, e-Stewards, or other applicable certifications. Partnership with local nonprofit organizations or local authorities: Specify whether the proposed e-waste collection activities involve collaboration with local nonprofit organizations or governmental authorities. Deadline for submission: Nov. 13, 2026 (date subject to change) Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov Technical Point of Contact: ThiThuyTien.Le@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated Request for Proposal solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

title: Sources Sought for the Recapitalization of the Navy�s High Voltage (230kV) Transmission Loop and all Ancillary Equipment at Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, GA
description: THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR EITHER A QUOTE OR PROPOSAL OR AN INVITATION FOR A BID. THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO RECAPITALIZE THE NAVY HIGH VOLTAGE 230KV TRANSMISSION LOOP AND ALL ANCILLARY EQUIPMENT AND GEAR AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE KINGS BAY, GEORGIA. THE WORK MUST COMPLY WITH ALL APPLICABLE NAVAL AND UTILITY PROVIDER PHYSICAL AND CYBERSECURITY REQUIREMENTS. IT REQUIRES SEAMLESS COORDINATION AND A SINGLE POINT OF ACCOUNTABILITY FOR EXECUTION WITHOUT UNNECESSARY SERVICE DISRUPTIONS OR DELAYS. NO SOLICITATION OR SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE CURRENTLY AVAILABLE. The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge of qualified and interested participants in any of the following categories. These include large business, small business, 8(a) business development participants, HUBZone small business concerns, service-disabled veteran-owned small business concerns, veteran-owned small business concerns, and women-owned small business concerns. Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, security-cleared personnel, security approvals, equipment, financial capability, and cybersecurity certifications relative to the project. The project entails utility infrastructure upgrades and connection facilities for the Navy-owned and operated 230kV electrical power transmission loop that services NSB Kings Bay, Georgia. The recapitalized infrastructure must be capable of safely and reliably interconnecting with the regional 230kV transmission grid. Prior experience in coordinating high-voltage interconnections with a regulated utility provider is an essential requirement. Capabilities including live-line interconnection work, secure supply chain management, and cybersecurity expertise (e.g., NERC CIP, DoD UFC 4-010-06 for Industrial Control Systems) are considered essential for the timely and cost-effective completion of the project without coordination delays or interoperability concerns. The Government contemplates an acquisition to accomplish the wholesale recapitalization and cybersecurity hardening of the Navy-owned high-voltage transmission line and associated gear at NSB Kings Bay, Georgia. The modernized on-base grid will remain solely under the operational control of the U.S. Navy and is intended to service only the installation. The system must be designed to safely coordinate with the regional transmission utility for grid stability and reliability at the point of interconnection. Work will include relocation of the high power loop and crossing tower across the North River to a geotechnically stable site. It includes replacement of conductors along the primary transmission corridor. The new installation must meet all required Department of Defense and industry cybersecurity standards. This includes the wholesale modernization of substation digital protective relays with utility-grade devices and the implementation of a secure, encrypted Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. The Government�s SCADA system must be capable of providing necessary operational coordination and data exchange with the utility provider�s dispatch center via a secure communications gateway. The contractor will replace closed circuit television metering transformers with fault monitoring capability. The work requires replacement of porcelain insulators, high-voltage bushings, surge arrestors, and ground-grid bonding systems ensuring compatibility with incoming power feed loads and feeds. The contractor must remove manual or gang-operated air disconnect switches at the entry bays of Substations 1 through 3. The project includes installation of smart supervisory-controlled Motor-Operated Disconnects and vacuum or SF6 circuit breakers equipped with high-speed differential bus and transformer protection schemes. It also requires wholesale modernization of substation digital protective relays utility-grade devices with full coordination between the encrypted installation Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) telemetry. All telemetry and relay configurations must comply with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (EIP) standards. They must also comply with applicable DoD Unified Facilities Criteria 4-010-06 for Industrial Control Systems (ICS) standards and ad-hoc compatibility with existing utility infrastructure as determined by the agency. The anticipated period of performance is approximately 900 calendar days from award. The estimated magnitude for this procurement is between $100,000,000 to $250,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) is 221122 for Electric Power Distribution with a small business size standard of 1,100 employees. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.101(c)(2), responses to this notice are not offers and the Government will not accept them to form a binding contract. Any information submitted by respondents to this notice is strictly voluntary. The Government will use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement of the subject requirement. Industry will be notified of the results of the market research via the pre-solicitation or synopsis notice as applicable. GPC owns and operates the regional 230kV transmission grid that provides bulk power to the NSB Kings Bay point of interconnection. Any contractor performing this work must deliver a system that meets all relevant industry standards for protection, control, and communications (e.g., NERC, IEEE) to ensure safe and reliable grid operations. The design must allow for the necessary exchange of telemetry and operational data with GPC to ensure grid stability, without requiring the use of any proprietary utility software, hardware, or protocols on the government-owned portion of the system. Interested and responsible parties experienced in wholesale high-voltage power line work in Tier 3 security military installations with all necessary credentials and accreditations for both applicable naval and regional integration and interoperability standards should identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement. We place special emphasis on cybersecurity specifications and supply chain security. Interested and responsible parties should use the attached questionnaire to respond to this notice. Responses to this notice must be submitted in electronic Adobe PDF format and attached to an email addressed to ryan.d.bell16.civ@us.navy.mil and rebecca.m.jones75.civ@us.navy.mil. The due date for responses is 1400 hours EDT on 13 November 2026. Responses received by the due date and time of this notice will be considered by the Government. Any questions submitted via email to the recipients identified above prior to the due date for responses will be considered. No additional questions will be addressed.
