The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. Proposal Submission Phase I proposals are due: 13 November 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time All proposal submissions shall be made in accordance with Section L of the solicitation. Phase I proposals must be submitted electronically through the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE). In accordance with Section L.3(b), Offerors shall email the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than five (5) working days prior to the proposal due date to request a DoD SAFE Drop-Off Request. Questions and Requests for Clarification Questions shall be submitted in accordance with Section L no later than: 14 October 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time Questions received after this date may not be answered. Government responses may be issued through solicitation questions and answers and/or formal solicitation amendment, as appropriate. Solicitation Documents and Restricted GFI See the Attachments/Links section below for the solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents associated with this RFP. Certain Government Furnished Information identified in Section J is authorized under Distribution Statement C and will not be publicly posted to SAM.gov. Authorized Offerors requiring access to these documents shall submit a written request by email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist. Following verification of the requester�s authorization to receive the material, the Government will transmit the applicable documents through DoD SAFE. -------------------------------- Amendment A00001 -------------------------------- The United States Coast Guard (USCG) hereby issues Amendment A00001 to Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001, originally issued on SAM.gov on September 30, 2026. Amendment A00001 is issued to provide the Government�s responses to questions received, incorporate a standardized document for future vendor question submissions, and provide advance notice regarding anticipated future solicitation revisions. Amendment A00001 incorporates Attachment 2, Questions and Government Responses v1, containing Government responses to Questions 1 through 53. Questions 1 through 46 provide responses to vendor inquiries submitted during the presolicitation phase under Presolicitation Notice USCG-RB-S-III-2026. Question 47 is a Government-drafted clarification confirming that CLIN 0006 and CLIN 1006 are distinct line items with seperate requirements; Offerors are directed to review Attachment C-4, List of Deliverables, for details. title: Vacuum Turbo Pumps
description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing Turbomolecular Pumping Stations. The Turbomolecular Pumping Station (TMPS) will replace the Agilent Technologies/Varian TPS-compact TV301 (Model: 969-8221M003), which contains the following components: TV301 turbomolecular pump, integrated controller, variable leak valve and dry scroll backing pump. The manufacturer (Agilent/Varian) has discontinued this item and ceased its support of the key components. This acquisition will aid AFMETCAL in maintaining support for a multitude of different high-vacuum and vacuum metrology calibration equipment across the Air Force. The new standard would support high-vacuum chambers, vacuum sensors, transducers, and other similar high-vacuum TMDE. The TMPS shall evacuate vacuum TMDE up to high-vacuum levels in absolute mode. Responses will assist AFMETCAL in determining the availability of qualified sources and the appropriate acquisition strategy. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. title: USCG Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III)
description: The United States Coast Guard (USCG) is issuing Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 70Z02326R93250001 for the Response Boat Small Third Generation (RB-S III). The Government intends to award up to four (4) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for the design, production, testing, delivery, and related supplies and services for the RB-S III and associated purpose-built trailers in accordance with the solicitation. The acquisition will recapitalize the aging fleet of 29-foot RB-S II platforms and includes boats, trailers, logistics support, technical documentation, configuration management, supply support, and other related requirements identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents are provided below under the Attachments/Links section of this notice. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the solicitation, all applicable attachments, and any subsequent amendments in their entirety. The anticipated IDIQ ordering period is ten (10) years, consisting of a two (2) year base ordering period and one eight (8) year option ordering period. Two-Phase Acquisition and Evaluation Process This solicitation uses a two-phase competitive acquisition and down-select process. Phase I: The Government will evaluate written proposals under the following factors in accordance with Section M of the solicitation: Factor I � Mission Effectiveness (Non-Price) Factor II � Production and Management (Non-Price) Factor III � Price Following the Phase I evaluation and best-value tradeoff, the Government may select up to four (4) Offerors for award of IDIQ contracts. Each Phase I awardee will receive an initial Delivery Order satisfying the contract minimum guarantee for the construction and delivery of one (1) demonstrator boat and trailer for participation in Phase II. Phase II: Phase I awardees will participate in a Government-conducted In-Water Demonstration lasting up to 90 calendar days. Phase II will evaluate: Factor IV � In-Water Demonstration (Non-Price) Factor III � Price (carries forward from Phase I, not a new price evaluation) Phase II is an independent evaluation. Phase I evaluation results, other than carrying the price evaluation forward, will not influence the Phase II evaluation. The Technical Evaluation Team (TET) will use the In-Water Demonstration Report and documented personal observations during the In-Water Demonstration to conduct a comparative evaluation of how each demonstrator boat performed in comparison to the other demonstrator boats. The TET will document the specific technical advantages and disadvantages identified through the comparative evaluation under Factor IV. Following completion of Phase II, the Government will conduct a final best-value tradeoff evaluation and select one (1) IDIQ contractor to receive all subsequent production Delivery Orders for the remaining RB-S III boats. Price evaluations will remain unchanged from Phase I; no price revisions or updates will be permitted in Phase II. Proposal Submission Phase I proposals are due: 13 November 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time All proposal submissions shall be made in accordance with Section L of the solicitation. Phase I proposals must be submitted electronically through the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE). In accordance with Section L.3(b), Offerors shall email the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than five (5) working days prior to the proposal due date to request a DoD SAFE Drop-Off Request. Questions and Requests for Clarification Questions shall be submitted in accordance with Section L no later than: 14 October 2026 at 1400 Eastern Time Questions received after this date may not be answered. Government responses may be issued through solicitation questions and answers and/or formal solicitation amendment, as appropriate. Solicitation Documents and Restricted GFI See the Attachments/Links section below for the solicitation and publicly releasable supporting documents associated with this RFP. Certain Government Furnished Information identified in Section J is authorized under Distribution Statement C and will not be publicly posted to SAM.gov. Authorized Offerors requiring access to these documents shall submit a written request by email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist. Following verification of the requester�s authorization to receive the material, the Government will transmit the applicable documents through DoD SAFE.

title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI � Ready Building, Fort Bliss, Texas DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding Design-Build to Budget (DBtB), project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support the upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The planned procurement will construct a Ready Building, Project Number 570628, at Biggs Army Airfield, Fort Bliss, El Paso, Texas. The project will provide a permanent, properly sized Ready Building supporting continuous, 24-hour operations for an on-call Air MEDEVAC crew. The facility will provide approximately 4,836 square feet of permanent single-story construction. The facility will provide operational space for a five-person aircraft crew, living and readiness space for one five-person crew, and surge capacity for an additional five-person crew. The facility must enable aircraft crews to remain postured for rapid response, with direct access to the aircraft parking apron for MEDEVAC launches and weekend aircraft maintenance. The existing temporary facility is undersized and is not adjacent to the aircraft parking apron. The existing facility will remain operational until construction of the new Ready Building is complete. The temporary facility is outside the new construction footprint and is included in the project demolition scope after completion of the new facility. The project site is adjacent to the Biggs Army Airfield aircraft parking apron. The project site is anticipated to fall within a seismic design condition that may result in Seismic Design Category D requirements. The final Seismic Design Category will be determined by the project Designer of Record in accordance with applicable codes and project-specific site conditions. The Ready Building is a Risk Category IV facility because of its emergency-response function. The project must comply with applicable Unified Facilities Criteria, antiterrorism/force-protection, fire/life-safety, seismic, cybersecurity, and installation requirements. Fort Bliss utility systems are privatized. Required services include electric power, natural gas or an approved alternative fuel approach, water, sanitary sewer, and telecommunications. Utility-system owners are anticipated to provide and own required connections to the facility service disconnect or other defined point of demarcation. The civil utility plan identifies a need for utility-owner rerouting of water and gas around the proposed lid pond. Budget & Schedule: Construction Cost Limitation (CCL): $7,200,000.00 Solicitation Release: 02 March 2027 Agreement Award: 21 May 2027 Construction Completion Date: 365 calendar days from Notice to Proceed Beneficial Occupancy Date: 05 July 2028 INSTRUCTIONS TO INDUSTRY Review Attached Project Information Packet (PIP) Interested firms are directed to review the attached document. This packet provides comprehensive project requirements, constraints, and the complete questionnaire reference. Submit Responses via Microsoft Forms To streamline the collection and analysis of industry feedback, responses to the market research questionnaire must be submitted electronically via the following link: Online Feedback Form: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/ZwqwSLBZpb Response Due Date: 13 NOVEMBER 2026 BY 2PM. All electronic responses must be submitted via the online form no later than: 13 NOVEMBER 2026 BY 2PM. title: Request for Information: Air Operations Center (AOC) Common Air Defense Picture (CADP)
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify existing and emerging software-enabled capabilities that can improve air and missile defense planning, situational awareness, reporting, readiness analysis, sustainment analysis, and decision support. Current workflows require personnel to consolidate information from multiple systems, data sources, and manual processes. This fragmentation can increase manual workload, delay access to relevant information, and complicate collaborative planning and decision support across command-and-control organizations. The Government seeks information on commercial capabilities that can improve access to authorized information, reduce manual reconciliation and reporting burden, and provide authorized users with a more integrated operational picture. The desired capability should support users operating at multiple echelons of command and control while preserving Government decision authority and existing authoritative command-and-control functions.

title: R702--National Longitudinal Survey and Data Management of Psychiatric and Social Health
description: SUBJECT: Notice of Intent to Sole Source National Longitudinal Survey and Data management of Psychiatric and Social Health DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to award, on a sole source basis, a non commercial, cost reimbursement (cost only, no fee) requirements contract to the University of Michigan, Survey Research Center (SRC), 1109 Geddes Ave Ste 3300, Ann Arbor, MI 48109 1015. The requirement is to design, program, and administer a national, longitudinal mental health survey using the Composite International Diagnostic Interview, fifth version (CIDI 5.0) for the VA Central Office, Homeless Programs Office (HPO), National Center on Homelessness Among Veterans (NCHAV). Services include survey instrument programming, mixed mode data collection (web/CATI), probability based sampling with Veteran oversampling, data security, quality assurance, and delivery of cleaned datasets and survey weights for baseline and follow up waves. RATIONALE SUMMARY: The University of Michigan is the only known responsible source with validated access to CIDI 5.0 and proven capability to program and administer this proprietary diagnostic instrument. Market research indicates that no other vendors possess the required CIDI 5.0 expertise or the ability to conduct a full probability national longitudinal survey with Veteran oversampling. Attempting to transition this work to another vendor would result in substantial duplication of cost and unacceptable delays. ESTIMATED VALUE: Approximately $6,000,000 over the five year period of performance. AUTHORITY: FAR 6.302 1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. RESPONSES: This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, parties who believe they can fully meet this requirement including validated access to CIDI 5.0 and the ability to execute a probability based national longitudinal survey with Veteran oversampling may submit a capability statement by the date/time listed in this posting. Capability statements must demonstrate the ability to meet all technical requirements. SUBMISSIONS: Email capability statements to: Ann Marie Stewart, Contracting Officer annmarie.stewart@va.gov Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. DISCLAIMER: A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses is solely at the Government s discretion. This notice does not constitute a solicitation. title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

title: Request for Information for U-2 Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System -2
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, manufacturing, engineering, software development, maintenance and experience to meet qualification requirements to repair and sustain the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS)-2 components and ground support equipment. The level of security clearance and amount of overseas continental united states participation in this requirement has not been determined. The Government does not own or have access to the data for ASARS-2 sensor. The Government has determined that this system is a noncommercial item. Contractor shall furnish all material, support equipment, tools, test equipment, and services. The contractor is responsible for providing, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at their facility or a subcontractor�s facility. Contractor furnished material or parts used for replacement shall equal or exceed the quality of the original material or parts. Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS) -2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval to Operate (ATO) package, Cybersecurity Authorization Package (CAP), Risk Management Framework (RMF), Interim Authority to Test (IATT), Interim Authority to Connect (ATC), and/or separate ATO, as applicable and requested by the Government. This effort also requires Depot Maintenance Support Teams (DMST) to support the following sustainment activities: mission software updates; Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) engineering; engineering change proposals; configuration management (hardware and software); integration with ASARS-related systems on the U-2 platform; data management; technical data (such as technical manuals and reports) development and maintenance; in-plant Specialized Repair Activity and sparing; technical and engineering actions for calibrating ASARS-2; resolving system failures/issues in a timely manner; and planning/preparation/implementation of system sustainment improvements.

title: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day
description: Domestic Aviation Design Industry Day Important Dates: Industry Day Registration Deadline -- 3:00 PM EDT on Friday, November 13, 2026 Industry Day -- 9:00 AM EDT on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 1. Introduction For over 10 years, TSA has held regular events to engage with external aviation security stakeholders, including airports, airport designers, airlines, equipment vendors, industry groups, and other domestic and international industry stakeholders in support of TSA�s mission. TSA has capitalized on these events to: Promote TSA�s checkpoint system of systems designs and standards; Encourage collaboration within the aviation security community; Share best practices from a variety of operating environments, facility sizes, and capabilities; Learn about the latest security technology advances and industry innovations; and Engage with stakeholders early in the design process to allow TSA to influence designs and support public-private partnerships. 2. Aviation industry associations; and h. Federal, state, and local government entities. To be considered for attendance, each responding organization must submit a one- to three-sentence summary describing its relevant experience and any other pertinent information demonstrating that it qualifies under one or more of the categories listed above. 6. Acceptance from TSA for attendance at this event is subject to TSA�s sole review and discretion. title: Solicitation_S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter
description: ***29 OCT 2026 - AMD 0004 issued*** ***20 OCT 2026 - AMD 0003 issued*** ***13 OCT 2026 - AMD 0002 issued*** ***10 SEP 2026 - AMD 0001 issued*** The Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) to establish a new five-year, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the manufacture and delivery of four (4) variants of the S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter. This is a non-commercial requirement. Requirement: The S-280C/G is a lightweight, tactical military shelter designed to house and protect sensitive electronic equipment and personnel. Manufacturing shall be in strict accordance with the Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) and ASTM E1975-22. The scope includes First Article Testing (FAT), production, and delivery of all associated technical and logistics data. National Stock Numbers (NSNs): 5411-01-304-3069 (Shielded) and 5411-01-092-0892 (Unshielded). Set-Aside: This is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The applicable size standard for NAICS 332311 is 750 employees. Award Basis: The Government intends to award a single IDIQ contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This will be a tradeoff source selection conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15. Contract Value: The minimum guaranteed value for this contract is $100,000.00. The maximum estimated contract ceiling is $4,000,000.00. Technical Data Package (TDP): The TDP for this solicitation is Export-Controlled (Distribution Statement C). To gain access, interested parties must have a current and valid DD Form 2345, "Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement" certification on file with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office (JCO). The TDP can be accessed through the attachments section of this announcement on SAM.gov by certified offerors. Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing to the points of contact listed below no later than September 24, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Points of Contact: Nicholas A. Lang, Contract Specialist, nicholas.a.lang.civ@army.mil Daniel J. Kamatics is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the KAron liner. KAron is a polyester, thermosetting, resin-based coating incorporating Teflon particles which is tailored to meet specific performance requirements, qualified to aviation military specifications and is trademarked and proprietary to Kamatics. No modifications, therefore, repairs, can be made by any personnel other than Kamatics personnel. The OEM exclusively possesses the requisite technical data, knowledge, and intellectual property necessary to apply KAron liner to the F/A-18 NLG Steering Collar as specified in the blueprint. title: National Architect-Engineer Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Contract
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice only. This notice does not constitute a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), Request for Proposals (RFP), or Invitation for Bids (IFB), nor does it represent a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. This Sources Sought Synopsis is issued solely for market research and planning purposes to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources. It is not a Request for Proposals or Quotes and imposes no obligation on the Government to acquire any goods or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government reserves the right to determine the appropriate acquisition approach based on the results of this market research. Responders should not anticipate feedback regarding their submissions. The Government will not pay for any costs incurred in responding to this Synopsis; all costs associated with responding are solely at the responding party's expense. The information provided herein is subject to change and is non-binding on the Government. The purpose of this notice is to conduct market research to identify potential and qualified sources, assess industry capabilities, and establish effective acquisition strategies, including potential small business set-aside opportunities. No reimbursement will be provided for any costs associated with submitting information in response to this announcement or any follow-up information requests. Overview The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is conducting market research to establish Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for comprehensive, multidisciplinary Architect-Engineer (A/E) services. These contracts are intended to provide integrated, sustainable, and adaptive design solutions across federally owned and leased real property nationwide. The Government anticipates awarding multiple contracts with multi-year ordering periods (5 year base with one 5 year option) to support GSA zones and client agencies across the United States and its territories. Expected typical project size is to be above the simplified acquisition threshold of $350,000. The potential place of performance for services rendered under this contract is on an as-needed basis for federal projects anywhere in the United States and its territories. This will require the capability to travel to GSA and other Government agency office locations nationwide. In some instances, performance of services is expected to require the capability for contractors to dispatch personnel to multiple locations simultaneously. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541310 (Architectural Services) & 541330 (Engineering Services), which has a small business size standard of $12.5 million and $25.5 million respectively. Scope of Services Services provided under the resulting IDIQ contracts will encompass a comprehensive range of professional A/E design and engineering disciplines. Scopes of work for individual task orders may include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Core Project Life Cycle Services - These services cover the entire project lifecycle, from initial concept to post-construction closeout. Planning and Pre-Design Feasibility, pre-design, and project development studies Master planning Cost Estimating Real Estate Market Analysis Assessment and Investigation Existing conditions surveys, and field investigation Building condition survey evaluation reports (exterior and interior) Environmental investigation, reviews, inventories, and audits Energy audits and studies Design and Documentation Concept design, Design development, and Construction document development (both architectural and engineering) Interior design, including Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FFE) Building standard documents Construction Support and Closeout Constructability review and evaluation Submittal and shop drawing review Management and inspection (M&I) services during construction and Construction inspection Building and system commissioning Post Construction Contract Services (PCCS); Record and close-out documents 2. Specialized Technical & System Design - Work requested often involves the assessment, repair, and upgrade of existing complex building systems. Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) Full MEP services, including design of HVAC systems and electrical systems and lighting Assessment and design for mechanical components (e.g., pumps, fans, air handlers, water distribution systems) and air distribution Design of water and waste water systems, including performance of sanitary inspections Temperature control assessment and design and BAS system assessment and integration Building Structure and Envelope Structural evaluation and design Fa�ade evaluation and remediation design Water infiltration investigation and mitigation design Safety, Security, and Compliance Fire and Life Safety evaluation and design Rehabs to improve energy efficiency and safety concerns Seismic & Blast protection and Vertical Transportation Code Compliance 3. Required AE Disciplines and Expertise - AE firms will need staff with licensed and/or specialized expertise in the following disciplines: Core Architectural and Engineering Disciplines Architecture and Interior Architecture Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Structural & Civil Engineering, and Plumbing Historic Preservation Specialized Expertise A Qualified/Licensed Fire Protection Engineer (NCEES)* Security Space Planning & Workplace Cost Estimating and Scheduling Environmental Services Modernization and Quality Control Building Information Modeling (BIM) Quality control review and Report writing Submission Requirements Interested firms are invited to submit a written Capability Statement. Submissions must not exceed five (5) pages in length and must address the following elements: A. Company Profile Official company name, street address, telephone number, and primary website URL. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code. Office location(s) and primary design production facilities. Business size status under NAICS 541310 or 541330 (Large Business or Small Business). Applicable SBA socio-economic certifications (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business [SDVOSB], Woman-Owned Small Business [WOSB], or Economically Disadvantaged WOSB [EDWOSB]). B. Relevant Experience Summarize three to five (3�5) relevant projects completed within the past ten (10) years. Demonstrate experience in projects of similar scale, scope, and complexity, such as federal workplace design, major repairs and alterations, or complex building systems. Include project title, customer/agency point of contact, contract value, role (Prime or Subcontractor), and a brief narrative of the work performed. C. Nationwide Capacity Demonstrate organizational capacity to manage and execute multiple task orders simultaneously across diverse geographic locations nationwide. Describe key disciplines maintained in-house versus those typically fulfilled through subcontractor or joint venture arrangements. Submission Instructions Responses must be submitted electronically via email to the primary procurement contacts listed below: Submission Deadline: Primary Contact: Point of Contact Email: Subject Line Format: Sources Sought Response - National A/E IDIQ - [Firm Name] Hard copies, telephonic inquiries, and late submissions will not be reviewed or acknowledged. All information provided in response to this notice will be used strictly for market research and acquisition planning purposes. This notice encourages participation from qualified small business concerns, including socio-economic program participants, to assist GSA in evaluating the feasibility of small business set-asides for this procurement. title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: In accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening � Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA), posted October 2, 2026, under Notice ID HQCAAA2701, the following requirement supports Area of Interest (AoI) 5.1 Accelerate Eligible Patron Growth. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for a digital storefront, in-store fulfillment, and delivery solution(s), hereinafter referred to as �DeCA2U�. The primary goal of DeCA2U is to deliver a seamless, modern, and fully integrated omnichannel grocery experience for authorized patrons at Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) locations in the contiguous United States (CONUS), Alaska, Hawaii, and Puerto Rico that matches or exceeds the best commercial grocery services available today. The DeCA2U solution shall utilize a market-aligned commercial financial model typical of leading grocery retailers. The prospective contractor shall identify all locations in which it could provide an entire end-to-end solution enabling authorized patrons to place grocery orders, make payment, and receive their groceries at a designated delivery location. Specifically, DeCA2U will provide one unified, easy-to-use platform enabling authorized patrons and military units to: Shop and order groceries online anytime, anywhere via mobile app or website; Receive accurate real-time inventory and pricing from their local commissary; Benefit from fast, accurate in-store picking and professional order assembly; Enjoy reliable, tracked doorstep delivery directly to their home or quarters or convenient curbside pickup; Track and be rewarded for purchases; Leverage value-added functionality like forgotten items, �People who bought this� recommendations, menu building, price checking, or any other shopping experience enhancement capability; and Complete transactions through a secure, seamless payment process supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT). The Government reserves the right to add payment options. Offerors shall propose pricing reflecting current commercial market rates for similar omnichannel. The Service Contract Labor Standards (formerly the Service Contract Act), 41 U.S.C. ��6701 et seq. will be applicable to any resulting contract. The desired outcome is to establish a long-term commercial partnership that provides authorized commissary patrons with a convenient, reliable, and cost-effective grocery shopping experience through an integrated solution for online ordering, payment processing, order fulfillment, pickup, and delivery. The solution should leverage proven commercial capabilities, support operational efficiency, enhance the commissary benefit, and provide a scalable and sustainable service model that can adapt to evolving mission requirements and patron needs. Proposed solutions should comply with applicable commercial and/or Department of War (DoW) cybersecurity standards, including but not limited to, SOC 2 Type 2. Additionally, integrated payment and entitlement gateways supporting all tender types including, but not limited to, MILITARY STAR and SNAP EBT. Proposed solutions must meet current commercial PCI DSS compliance and USDA Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) digital security specifications. The platform shall ensure robust end-to-end encryption for data at rest and in transit (FIPS 140-3 validated) and secure patron Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in accordance with federal privacy standards. Solutions shall propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflects customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, and delivery benchmarks for the proposed capability. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government�s discretion. DeCA will not endorse any contractor employee for the purpose of installation access; as such, solutions shall address their proposed approach to meeting applicable military installation access requirements, including personnel screening, credentialing, and delivery access procedures. DeCA will utilize the phased evaluation process established in the overarching Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), Notice ID HQCAAA2701. Interested vendors with demonstrated commercial experience in grocery eCommerce, order fulfillment, pickup, delivery, or integrated retail solutions with foundational information security management system standard should submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in accordance with the applicable submission requirements of the overarching CSO. Solution Briefs should describe: the proposed commercial approach; relevant capabilities; anticipated benefits to DeCA and its authorized patrons; proposed business model; PoP; Service Contract Labor Standards; installation access; and cybersecurity measures. Additionally, all proposed solutions shall address the vendor's ability to integrate with DeCA�s retail ecosystems and scale to DeCA�s business needs. The Government will evaluate submissions in accordance with the criteria established in the overarching CSO and may invite selected vendors to participate in subsequent phases. The closing date for this �Call for Solution� is Friday 13 November 2026 at 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). All communications, including solution brief information and submission requirements shall be sent via email to the following Points of Contact: Diana Gross-Bendall, email: diana.gross-bendall@deca.mil and Tinitia Gholson, email: tinitia.gholson@deca.mil.

title: Sensitive But Unclassified-Encrypted (SBU-E) Radio Cybersecurity Industry Day
description: The Department of the Army, representing the Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (CPE C2IN), the Project Manager Command and Control Transport (PM C2T), and the Product Manager Tactical Communication Systems (PdM TCS), has issued a Call for Solutions (CFS) under Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Part 212.70 to establish a 10-year enterprise acquisition framework for innovative tactical communication capabilities. The Army will host an Industry Day event from 1-3 December 2026 to facilitate collaboration and information sharing regarding upcoming security requirements for Sensitive But Unclassified-Encrypted (SBU-E) tactical radios. The primary objective is to brief industry partners on new cybersecurity requirements for SBU-E tactical radios and to provide a collaborative forum for feedback. Participation is limited to federal government employees, support contractors, and industry partners with current federal contracts (FEDCON). Industry partners must limit attendance to three attendees per company. See attachment for more details.
